nodes.referent: Søren Aabye Kierkegaard (1813-1855), the Danish philosopher, theologian, and social critic based in Copenhagen, author of Either/Or, Fear and Trembling, The Concept of Anxiety, and The Sickness Unto Death, standardly credited as the earliest and most direct 19th-century precursor of existentialist philosophy through his focus on individual subjective existence, anxiety, and the leap of faith -- not any other person named Kierkegaard, and not the Kierkegaard research institutes/societies that bear his name.

nodes.referent: Jean-Paul Charles Aymard Sartre (1905-1980), the French philosopher, playwright, novelist, and public intellectual, author of Being and Nothingness (1943) and the 1945 lecture Existentialism Is a Humanism, the philosopher most closely associated in the public mind with 20th-century (specifically postwar French) existentialism, longtime partner of Simone de Beauvoir -- not any other person named Sartre.

nodes.referent: Martin Heidegger (1889-1976), the German philosopher of Messkirch, professor at Freiburg and Marburg, author of Being and Time (1927) and The Question Concerning Technology (1954), whose phenomenological/hermeneutic ontology profoundly reshaped 20th-century Continental philosophy, despite Heidegger's own explicit rejection of the 'existentialist' label (notably in his Letter on Humanism, responding to Sartre) -- not any other person surnamed Heidegger.

nodes.referent: Gabriel Honore Marcel (1889-1973), the French philosopher, playwright, and music critic, a Catholic convert whose own philosophy of being, participation, and intersubjectivity (Metaphysical Journal, 1927; Being and Having) is usually classed as 'Christian existentialism,' though Marcel himself preferred 'Neo-Socratic' and resisted the existentialist label for his own work; standardly credited with applying the term 'existentialist' to Jean-Paul Sartre's philosophy in the mid-1940s -- not any other person named Gabriel Marcel.

nodes.rationale: Ordered this wave as the philosopher credited with naming the movement; the node itself is well-justified independent of that framing -- Marcel is a substantial, independently notable 20th-century philosopher with his own body of work predating and running parallel to Sartre's -- so the node is proposed even though (see companion edges file and report.md) I decline the order's suggested founded_or_formalized grain for the edge.
